sections.h2: Where is the Bradley County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The Bradley County Register of Deeds is at 155 N. Ocoee Street, Suite 102, Cleveland, TN 37311, and the phone is 423-728-7240. The county's page names Missy Mathews as Register.

Recording in Tennessee happens at the county level, so a deed for any house in Bradley County goes to this one office, whether the property is in Cleveland, in Charleston or in the unincorporated hills between them. The county page does not post a fee schedule or hours, so call before you drive over with a deed, and ask for the total recording charge for your page count.

sections.h2: How do you search Bradley County land records online?
sections.html:
Bradley County points searchers to TitleSearcher, a vendor site that the county says gives online access to land records 24 hours a day, seven days a week. The images and index data cover deeds, mortgages, releases, powers of attorney, restrictions, plat maps and other document types filed at the register's office.

The register's page also links a property fraud alert sign-up. Fraud alerts watch for new filings under your name, which matters if you own rental property, inherited land or a vacant lot that you rarely visit. Someone who forges a deed against an empty house tends to count on the owner not noticing.

Before listing, pull the vesting deed for your parcel and check three things: the spelling of every owner name, the legal description, and any deed of trust that was never released. A lender that was paid off but did not file a release leaves a cloud on title, and a closing agent will ask you to clear it.

sections.h2: What taxes apply when a deed is recorded in Bradley County?
sections.html:
The taxes are set by state law and apply in every Tennessee county. The Tennessee Department of Revenue lists a realty transfer tax of $0.37 per $100 and a mortgage tax of $0.115 per $100 of indebtedness, with the first $2,000 of the debt exempt.

ItemRule
Realty transfer tax$0.37 per $100 of the greater of price or value
Who pays itThe grantee (buyer) named on the deed
Mortgage tax$0.115 per $100 of debt, first $2,000 exempt, paid by the borrower
Required statement on debt instrumentsMaximum principal indebtedness for Tennessee recording tax purposes
Register receipt feeUp to $1 per receipt for each tax
Penalty for unpaid indebtedness tax$250 or double the unpaid tax, whichever is greater

Source: Tennessee Department of Revenue, Recordation Tax Manual. On a $230,000 sale, the transfer tax is 2,300 hundreds times $0.37, or $851. That example is arithmetic, not a quote from Bradley County, so ask the title agent for the exact charge on your deal.

sections.h2: Who is exempt from the Tennessee realty transfer tax?
sections.html:
The state manual excludes a short list of transfers. Several are common in estates, divorces and family moves, which are situations where sellers often call a buyer for a fast sale.

  • Deeds an executor signs to carry out a devise in a will.
  • Domestic settlement decrees and deeds that adjust property rights between divorcing parties.
  • A conveyance from one spouse to the other that creates or dissolves a tenancy by the entirety.
  • Transfers into a revocable living trust by the person who made it, and transfers back to that person or the spouse.
  • Real estate formerly held by tenants in common, and the release of a life estate to the remainder beneficiaries.
  • Transfers to or from a government entity.

No oath of consideration is needed on an exempt transfer. On a taxable deed, the buyer swears to the price or value on the face of the deed in front of the register, and the state can check that figure against the assessor's value later.

sections.h2: How does Bradley County assess value for the oath on a deed?
sections.html:
For a sale between unrelated parties, the price paid is the usual figure. The state accepts the tax base listed at the local assessor's office, or a recent appraisal the assessor has accepted, as the fair market value when value drives the tax. Anything lower can be audited, assessed and charged penalties and interest.

The Bradley County Assessor of Property, Stanley Thompson, is at the Courthouse Annex, 155 Broad Street NW, Room 105, and the phone is 423-728-7125. The office runs a Tennessee property viewer for parcel data and tax maps. Check the assessor's number for your house before you sign a deed that states a value far from it.

sections.h2: What is Bradley County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 115,465 residents in July 2025 and 47,861 housing units on 328.76 square miles of land. Median owner-occupied home value for 2020 to 2024 is $261,900, owner-occupancy is 67.3 percent, and median household income is $66,552. Median gross rent is $1,030, which matters for a landlord weighing a sale against holding.

Cleveland is the county seat and largest city. Charleston is the other city, and the Hiwassee River forms the county's northern border. Wikipedia notes that the Cherokee Agency moved to Charleston in 1821, that Cleveland was chosen as county seat in 1836 and that the county ranks second in Tennessee for poultry and broilers. Whirlpool, Mars, Procter and Gamble and Duracell are among the manufacturers it names around Cleveland.

Public schools split between Bradley County Schools and Cleveland City Schools. Lee University and Cleveland State Community College are in the county. Ridges run north-northeast through the county, and Candies Creek Ridge crosses Cleveland, so lots on slopes need a careful survey and drainage check before a buyer's lender signs off.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Bradley County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is at 155 N. Ocoee Street, Suite 102, Cleveland, TN 37311. The phone is 423-728-7240, and the county's page names Missy Mathews as Register.

faqs.q: Can I search Bradley County deeds from home?
faqs.a: Yes. The county directs people to TitleSearcher, which offers land record images and index data around the clock. The register's page also links a property fraud alert sign-up.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax in Bradley County?
faqs.a: It is $0.37 per $100 of the sale price or value, the same in every Tennessee county. The buyer named on the deed is responsible for it, and the register collects it at recording.

faqs.q: Do I pay mortgage tax if I sell for cash?
faqs.a: No mortgage tax applies when no loan is recorded. The tax is $0.115 per $100 of debt above the first $2,000 and is charged on instruments such as a deed of trust. A cash purchase has no deed of trust.

faqs.q: Does the register fix errors in my deed?
faqs.a: The register records documents as they are presented. Ask the title company or attorney who drafted the deed how to correct it, and call 423-728-7240 to confirm what the office needs to accept the corrected version.
